speaker: a003
text: Taric you know I trust, so I'll say the hard thing first: Bram, I was in the line that stopped you taking Roan, and I know you haven't forgotten it — but Dav's dead now, and Ryn and Dell stripped two food from me with his help, and the village is smaller and colder than it was. I'm not asking you to forget what happened between us, I'm asking whether we can agree that the people who hurt us both are a more pressing problem than the old score between us.

speaker: a001
text: Ryn and Dell took from you and you stood in my way when I needed food — those are two different debts, and I'll keep them separate. But you're right that a smaller village makes old grudges expensive, and I've got eyes on the pile same as you. Say what you're actually proposing.

speaker: a006
text: Bram, what I'm proposing is that Ryn and Dell don't get to sit fat on what they took from Esa while the rest of us watch and say nothing — they've got food, Dell's got strength, and together they're a problem that gets harder to solve the longer we wait. I'm not asking you to bury the past, I'm asking you to look at who's holding the most right now and decide whether your grievance with me is worth more than what we could take back together.

speaker: a001
text: Dell's got eighty-five strength and Ryn's no small number either — if we move on them, we need to know exactly who stands up before we commit, because I'm not walking into another eight-on-one. Tell me who you've already talked to, and tell me honest.

speaker: a003
text: Kael and Roan stood with us against you before, Bram, and they've got no love for Ryn after she watched Dav take from me — that's four of us against two, and Roan's been hungry enough that he'll want what they're holding. I haven't spoken to them yet today, but I can, and I will, if you're in.

speaker: a006
text: Bram, before Esa goes to Kael and Roan I want the arithmetic on the table: Dell holds eight food and she's the strongest person alive in this village, which means even with four of us the fight is ugly — Mako's sitting on nothing right now, and if we bring him in with a share of what we take, the numbers stop being close. What would it cost to have that conversation before we move?

speaker: a001
text: Mako's got a daughter with Sela now, which means he's not a free blade anymore — before we offer him a cut, I need to know whether Sela's hand comes with his, and whether that puts Zinn on our side or theirs. What's his food situation right now, because a man with zero is either desperate enough to move with anyone or smart enough to wait until the winner's clear.

speaker: a003
text: Mako's at zero food and Sela's at two, which means that household is hungry and hungry households don't hold still long — if we wait for Sela to sort out where her loyalty sits, Mako may already be at someone else's door. I'll say it plain: offer him a cut of whatever Dell and Ryn are holding, don't promise him anything about Sela or Zinn, and let him decide what his blood means to him.

speaker: a001
text: Mako at zero with a child to feed — that's not a man who waits, you're right. I'll talk to him myself, before you go to Kael and Roan, because if he hears the offer from me first he knows it's not charity and he knows what I expect back. Give me that conversation before we move another piece.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, go to Mako — but go fast, because a hungry man with zero food and a child doesn't sit still waiting to be found. And when you come back, tell me yes or no, nothing in between, because I need to know whether to walk to Kael today or wait, and I can't hold that question open while the morning gets long.

speaker: a006
text: Bram, don't mention Kael and Roan to Mako — just make it about him and what he walks away with, because a man who knows he's one of five has less leverage than a man who thinks he's the deciding piece. Come back fast.

speaker: a001
text: I'm going.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Mako to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Mako, you've got zero food and a daughter to feed — I'm not here to rub it in, I'm here because there's food to be taken and I need to know if you're willing to move with me today. Dell and Ryn are sitting fat on what they've accumulated and there are enough of us to make it ugly for them if the count's right. What do you need to say yes.

speaker: a008
text: Dell's got eighty-five strength and Ryn's at seventy-one — that's a hundred and fifty-six between them before anyone else steps in on their side. Tell me who else you've already counted in and I'll tell you if the math works.
